notebook_exported.location: Notebook tab → Export as Markdown: status-bar success message after the notebook was written as Markdown; {count} is the number of cells, and each result table preview was limited to 50 rows.
notebook_exported.value: Se exportaron {count} celdas; las vistas previas de resultados se limitaron a 50 filas

notebook_exported_ipynb.location: SQL Editor → Notebook → Export Jupyter: status-bar success message after the notebook was saved as a Jupyter .ipynb file; {count} is the number of cells, {path} the file written.
notebook_exported_ipynb.value: Se exportaron {count} celdas como cuaderno de Jupyter a {path}

notebook_open_disk_unavailable.location: Browser-hosted SQLLY → Open Notebook action: message shown because local notebook files cannot be opened from disk.
notebook_open_disk_unavailable.value: Abrir archivos del disco no está disponible

notebook_open_failed.location: File menu → Open Notebook: status-bar error shown when the chosen notebook file cannot be read from disk; {error} is the system error.
notebook_open_failed.value: No se pudo abrir el cuaderno: {error}

notebook_save_failed.location: Workbench → Save Notebook or Save Notebook As: error shown when the notebook file cannot be written; {error} is the filesystem error.

notebook_save_unavailable.location: Browser preview → Notebook tab → Save Notebook: status-bar error shown in the web version, where a notebook cannot be saved to a file.
notebook_save_unavailable.value: Guardar en un archivo no está disponible

notebook_saved_to_path.location: Workbench → Save Notebook or Save Notebook As: success status showing the written notebook path in {path}.

open_disk_unavailable.location: Browser preview → File menu → Open SQL File: feature name inserted into the “not available in the browser” status-bar error when opening a SQL file from disk in the web version.
open_disk_unavailable.value: Abrir archivos del disco no está disponible

open_export_prompt.location: File menu → Open SQLLY Export → System open panel: confirm-button label (and prompt) of the native file chooser used to pick a .sqllyexport results snapshot; imperative.

open_export_unavailable.location: Browser preview → File menu → Open SQLLY Export: feature name inserted into the “not available in the browser” status-bar error when opening a .sqllyexport file in the web version.
open_export_unavailable.value: Abrir archivos de exportación de SQLLY no está disponible

open_failed.location: Open Project File picker → Status bar error: status-bar error shown when the SQL file chosen in the project-file picker cannot be read from disk; {path} is the file path, {error} the system error.

open_folder_prompt.location: File menu → Open Folder → System open panel: confirm-button label (and prompt) of the native folder chooser that sets the project folder for the project-file picker; imperative.

open_folder_unavailable.location: Browser preview → File menu → Open Folder: feature name inserted into the “not available in the browser” status-bar error when opening a project folder in the web version.

open_notebook_prompt.location: File menu → Open Notebook → System open panel: confirm-button label (and prompt) of the native file chooser used to pick a SQLLY notebook file; imperative.

open_project_first.location: Command palette → Project Folder: Git Changes: status-bar notice shown when no project folder is open yet, telling the user to use File › Open Folder… first; keep the menu path matching the translated menu.
open_project_first.value: Abre primero una carpeta de proyecto (Archivo › Abrir carpeta…)

open_sql_prompt.location: File menu → Open SQL File → System open panel: confirm-button label (and prompt) of the native file chooser used to open a .sql file into a new query tab; imperative.

readonly_export_context.location: Results panel → Snapshot banner: banner text above the grid when a .sqllyexport file is opened as a read-only results snapshot; {path} is the export file path, separated by a middle dot.
readonly_export_context.value: Exportación de SQLLY de solo lectura · {path}

readonly_export_opened.location: File menu → Open SQLLY Export: status-bar success message after a .sqllyexport file opened in a new read-only tab; {title} is the tab title taken from the file name.
readonly_export_opened.value: Exportación de SQLLY abierta en modo de solo lectura: {title}

recent_file_missing.location: Tab bar context menu → Recent Files: status-bar warning shown when a chosen recent file no longer exists and was dropped from the list; {path} is the missing file path.
recent_file_missing.value: {path} ya no existe; se eliminó de los archivos recientes

redis_certificate_directory_failed.location: File menu → Import From Other Tools → Redis Insight import: status-bar error shown when the folder for the export’s certificates and keys cannot be created; {path} is the folder, {error} the system error.

redis_import_failed.location: File menu → Import From Other Tools → Redis Insight import: status-bar error shown when the converted Redis Insight connections cannot be saved to SQLLY; {error} is the reason.
redis_import_failed.value: No se importó la exportación de Redis Insight: {error}

redis_import_prepare_failed.location: File menu → Import From Other Tools → Redis Insight import: status-bar error shown when the Redis Insight connections cannot be converted for import, an internal preparation failure; {error} is the reason.
redis_import_prepare_failed.value: No se pudo preparar la importación: {error}

redis_import_skipped.location: File menu → Import From Other Tools → Redis Insight import: sentence appended to the import result for each connection left out; {name} is the Redis Insight connection name, {reason} why it was skipped.

redis_import_summary.location: File menu → Import From Other Tools → Redis Insight import: status-bar result assembled from parts when no certificates were saved; {summary} is the import summary, {skipped} the skipped-connection sentences, {notes} extra notes.

redis_import_summary_certificates.location: File menu → Import From Other Tools → Redis Insight import: status-bar result when TLS certificates/keys were saved; {summary} import summary, {certificates} folder they were saved to, {skipped} skipped sentences, {notes} extra notes.

reload_failed.location: Query editor → File changed on disk alert → Reload: status-bar error shown when the changed SQL file cannot be read back into the tab; {error} is the system error.

result_save_failed.location: Workbench → Save Results export: error shown when the selected result file cannot be written; {error} is the filesystem or exporter error.

results_saved.location: File menu → Save Results: status-bar and notification-center success message after all result rows were written; {format} is the export format name (e.g. JSON), {path} the saved file path.

results_saved_truncated.location: File menu → Save Results: status-bar warning after saving when the result exceeded the row cap and only the first rows were written; {format} format name, {path} file path, {count} the row cap.
results_saved_truncated.value: {format} guardado en {path} (primeras {count} filas; el resultado era más grande)

save_browser_unavailable.location: Browser preview → File menu → Save SQL: status-bar error shown in the web version, where the query cannot be saved to a file but stays in the browser session.
save_browser_unavailable.value: Guardar en un archivo no está disponible (el texto de la consulta se conserva en la sesión del navegador)

save_data_exporting.location: Database Explorer → Table context menu → Save Data As (CSV, Excel, SQLLY export): busy status-bar message shown while the table rows are read and written; {identifier} is the qualified table name.

save_data_no_connection.location: Database Explorer → Table context menu → Save Data As (CSV, Excel, SQLLY export): status-bar error shown when no connection is active, so the table data cannot be read.

save_data_query_failed.location: Database Explorer → Table context menu → Save Data As (CSV, Excel, SQLLY export): status-bar error shown when the SELECT reading the table cannot be started; {error} is the server or connection message.

save_data_saved.location: Database Explorer → Table context menu → Save Data As: status-bar and notification-center success message after all table rows were saved; {rows} rows written, {identifier} qualified table name, {path} file path.

save_data_saved_truncated.location: Database Explorer → Table context menu → Save Data As: success message when the table hit the row cap, so only the first rows were saved; {rows} rows written, {identifier} table, {path} file, {count} the cap (10,000).
save_data_saved_truncated.value: Se guardaron {rows} filas de {identifier} en {path} (primeras {count} filas)

save_data_write_failed.location: Database Explorer → Table context menu → Save Data As (CSV, Excel, SQLLY export): status-bar error shown when the read table data cannot be written to the chosen file; {path} is the file path, {error} the system error.

save_failed.location: File menu → Save SQL: status-bar error shown when the query editor text cannot be written to its .sql file; {error} is the system error.

saved_to_path.location: File menu → Save SQL: status-bar success message after the query editor text was written to its .sql file (existing file or newly chosen path); {path} is the file path.

schema_docs_fallback_title.location: Command palette → Document Schema (Markdown): fallback heading used at the top of the generated schema documentation when no connection name is available; noun.

schema_docs_no_model.location: Command palette → Document Schema (Markdown): status-bar notice shown when no schema model has been loaded yet, asking the user to connect and wait for it to load.
schema_docs_no_model.value: Aún no hay un modelo de esquema cargado: conéctate y espera a que cargue el modelo de datos

schema_docs_save_failed.location: Command palette → Document Schema (Markdown): status-bar error shown when the generated schema documentation file(s) cannot be written; {error} is the system error.
schema_docs_save_failed.value: No se pudo guardar la documentación del esquema: {error}

schema_docs_saved_multiple.location: Command palette → Document Schema (Markdown): success message when a large schema was split into an index plus one file per schema; {path} is the main file path, {count} the number of files written.
schema_docs_saved_multiple.value: Documentación del esquema guardada en {path} ({count} archivos)

schema_docs_saved_single.location: Command palette → Document Schema (Markdown): status-bar and notification-center success message after the schema documentation was written as a single Markdown file; {path} is the file path.

schema_docs_unavailable.location: Browser preview → Command palette → Document Schema (Markdown): feature name inserted into the “not available in the browser” status-bar error when saving schema documentation in the web version.
schema_docs_unavailable.value: Guardar la documentación del esquema en un archivo no está disponible

script_generated.location: Database Explorer → Table context menu → Script As / Save Data As: status-bar success message after the data script opened in a new query tab; {kind} is “INSERT”, “MERGE” or the translated “temp table”.

script_generating.location: Database Explorer → Table context menu → Script As / Save Data As: busy status-bar message while the table rows are read to build a script; {kind} is INSERT, MERGE or “temp table”, {table} the qualified table name.

script_kind_temp_table.location: Database Explorer → Table context menu → Save Data As → temp table script: lowercase noun inserted as {kind} into the “Generating … script” and “… script generated” status-bar messages.

script_no_connection.location: Database Explorer → Table context menu → Script As / Save Data As (INSERT, MERGE, temp table): status-bar error shown when no connection is active, so the script cannot be generated.

script_query_failed.location: Database Explorer → Table context menu → Script As / Save Data As (INSERT, MERGE, temp table): status-bar error shown when the SELECT reading the rows cannot be started; {error} is the server message.

connect_first.location: Results → Grid → Cell context menu → Open Referenced Row: status-bar notice shown when the command is used but no connection is active; short imperative.
connect_first.value: Conéctate a una base de datos para seguir claves foráneas.

not_foreign_key.location: Results → Grid → Cell context menu → Open Referenced Row: status-bar notice shown when the clicked column is not part of a foreign key; {column} is the column name.
not_foreign_key.value: La columna {column} no es una clave foránea.

null_value.location: Results → Grid → Cell context menu → Open Referenced Row: status-bar notice shown when the clicked foreign-key cell is NULL, so there is no referenced row to open; keep “NULL” as the SQL keyword.
null_value.value: No se puede seguir un valor NULL de clave foránea.

opened.location: Results → Grid → Cell context menu → Open Referenced Row: status-bar message after a new query tab opened and ran a SELECT for the referenced parent row; {schema} and {table} name the referenced table.

diff_header.location: Query editor → History panel → Compare with current: first line of the read-only diff text opened in a new tab, introducing the line-by-line differences between the chosen saved version and the current editor text.
diff_header.value:
-- Versión comparada con el búfer actual.
-- Las líneas que empiezan con - solo están en la versión; las que empiezan con +, solo en el búfer actual.

diff_tab_title.location: Query editor → History panel → Compare with current: name of the new query tab that opens holding the diff between a saved version and the current editor text; short tab label.

diff_truncated.location: Query editor → History panel → Compare with current: note appended at the end of the diff tab when the comparison exceeded the line limit and the remaining differences were cut off.
diff_truncated.value: -- (diferencias truncadas: los documentos son muy grandes)

disabled.location: Workbench → Status bar: info message shown when the user tries to open a query tab's History panel while query version history is turned off in Settings.
disabled.value: El historial de versiones de consultas está desactivado (Preferencias > Editor > Historial de consultas)

results_unavailable_sql_restored.location: Workbench → Status bar: warning shown after restoring a saved query version whose stored results could not be loaded; the version's SQL was restored into the editor but its results were not.
results_unavailable_sql_restored.value: No se pudieron cargar los resultados guardados de esta versión; solo se restauró el SQL.

toggle_disabled.location: Workbench → Toggle Query History action: status shown when query history is disabled in preferences.

version_not_found.location: Workbench → Status bar: warning shown when comparing a History panel version with the current editor text fails because that saved version no longer exists.
version_not_found.value: Esa versión ya no está en el historial

version_unavailable.location: Workbench → Status bar: info message shown when restoring a version from the History panel fails because the version was deleted or evicted between the click and the restore.
version_unavailable.value: Esa versión ya no está disponible.

viewing_results_banner.location: Results → Historical results banner: strip above the read-only results restored with an older query version; {timestamp} is when that version was saved; tells the user to run the query to get fresh results.
viewing_results_banner.value: Viendo resultados de {timestamp}: ejecuta para actualizar

connect.location: Workbench → Status bar: info message shown when a Maintenance action (VACUUM, ANALYZE, REINDEX and similar) is chosen in the Object Explorer context menu but no connection can be resolved; asks the user to connect first.
connect.value: Conéctate a una base de datos para ejecutar el mantenimiento

list_failed.location: Workbench → Status bar: error shown when a database-wide Maintenance action could not read the list of tables it runs per table; {operation} is the maintenance operation name, {error} the server error.
list_failed.value: No se pudieron listar las tablas para {operation}: {error}

listing_tables.location: Workbench → Status bar: busy message while a database-wide Maintenance action first reads the table list to build one statement per table; {operation} is the maintenance operation name (for example ANALYZE TABLE).

script_failed.location: Workbench → Status bar: error shown when the SQL for an Object Explorer Maintenance action could not be generated; {operation} is the maintenance operation name, {error} the reason.

scripted.location: Workbench → Status bar: info message after a Maintenance action’s Script form opens its statement in a new query tab for review (nothing runs yet); {operation} is the maintenance operation name.
scripted.value: {operation}: script generado en una pestaña nueva; revísalo antes de ejecutarlo

unsupported.location: Workbench → Status bar: error shown when the chosen Object Explorer Maintenance action has no equivalent statement for this database engine at the selected object level (database, table, or index).
unsupported.value: Esta operación de mantenimiento no está disponible en este motor

production_rejected.location: Workbench → Status bar: error shown when a query proposed by an external AI agent through the MCP server targeted a production connection and was automatically rejected; MCP never drives production connections.
production_rejected.value: Las conexiones de producción nunca se controlan mediante MCP.

query_opened.location: Workbench → Status bar: info message after a read-only query proposed by an external AI agent through the MCP server is opened in a new query tab for the user to review and run.
query_opened.value: Se abrió una consulta desde un cliente MCP

columns_failed.location: Workbench → Status bar: error shown when Object Explorer → Generate Model could not read a table’s or view’s columns; {object} is the schema-qualified object name, {error} the reason.
columns_failed.value: No se pudieron leer las columnas de {object}: {error}

connect.location: Workbench → Status bar: info message shown when Object Explorer → Generate Model is used but no connection can be resolved for the selected node; asks the user to connect first.
connect.value: Conéctate a una base de datos para generar un modelo

copied.location: Workbench → Status bar: success message after Object Explorer → Generate Model copied the generated model code to the clipboard; {language} is the target language name (for example C# or TypeScript).

credentials_unresolved.location: Object Explorer → Generate Model (single table or view): error text, shown inside the column-read failure status message, when the saved credentials for the node’s connection could not be loaded; {error} is the reason.
credentials_unresolved.value: No se pueden resolver las credenciales: {error}

generating.location: Workbench → Status bar: busy message while Object Explorer → Generate Model reads one table’s or view’s columns; {language} is the target language, {object} the schema-qualified object name.

generating_scope.location: Workbench → Status bar: busy message while Generate Model builds models for every table in a schema or database; {language} is the target language, {scope} the schema or database name.
generating_scope.value: Generando {language} para todas las tablas de {scope}…

list_failed.location: Workbench → Status bar: error shown when Generate Model for a whole schema or database could not list its tables; {scope} is the schema or database name, {error} the reason.
list_failed.value: No se pudieron listar las tablas de {scope}: {error}

no_tables.location: Workbench → Status bar: warning shown when Generate Model for a schema or database found no tables to model; {scope} is the schema or database name.

none_generated.location: Workbench → Status bar: warning shown when Generate Model for a schema or database produced no models because every table failed to load; {skipped} is the number of tables skipped.
none_generated.value: No se generó ningún modelo: no se pudieron leer {skipped} tabla(s)

opened.location: Workbench → Status bar: success message after Generate Model opened the generated code in a new query tab; {language} is the target language, {name} the new tab’s file-style name (for example orders.cs).

opened_with_skips.location: Workbench → Status bar: warning after schema- or database-wide Generate Model opened its code but some tables failed; {language} is the target language, {count} the tables modeled, {skipped} the tables skipped.
opened_with_skips.value: {language} para {count} tabla(s) abierto; no se pudieron leer {skipped} tabla(s)

scope_credentials_unresolved.location: Workbench → Object Explorer → Generate Models for schema or database: error shown when saved credentials cannot be resolved; {error} is the credential-store error.

select_object.location: Workbench → Status bar: info message shown when Generate Model is invoked on an Object Explorer node that has no table or view name; asks the user to select a table or view.
select_object.value: Primero selecciona una tabla o vista en el explorador

ai_pending.location: Confirm Data Changes dialog → AI review area: dimmed text shown while the required AI review of the data-changing statement is still being generated; the Execute button stays disabled until it arrives.

cancel.location: Confirm Data Changes dialog → footer: button that cancels the pending INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or other data-changing statement without running it.

execute.location: Confirm Data Changes dialog → footer: warning-styled button that runs the reviewed data-changing statement; disabled while a required AI review is pending.

production_title.location: Confirm Data Changes dialog → Title bar (production): title used instead of the normal one when the statement about to change data targets a connection marked as production.
production_title.value: Confirmar cambios de datos en producción

title.location: Confirm Data Changes dialog → Title bar (non-production): title of the confirmation shown before running a data-changing statement (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE and similar) on a non-production connection.

unbounded_warning.location: Confirm Data Changes dialog → Missing WHERE warning: red warning under the SQL preview shown when the UPDATE or DELETE has no WHERE clause limiting the rows, so it may affect every row in the table.
unbounded_warning.value: Esta instrucción no tiene una cláusula WHERE que limite las filas. Revisa cuidadosamente las filas afectadas antes de ejecutarla.

ddl.location: Query tab → DDL side panel divider: label on the collapsed vertical strip to the right of the editor (letters stacked one per line, so keep very short); click to reopen the object-definition panel.

history.location: Query tab → History side panel divider: label on the collapsed vertical strip to the right of the editor (letters stacked one per line, so keep very short); click to reopen the version-history panel.

restore_editor.location: Query tab → Collapsed editor bar: small button beside the one-line SQL preview shown while the results pane is maximized; restores the normal editor and results split.

results.location: Query tab → Results divider: label on the collapsed horizontal strip between the editor and the results pane; click it to expand the results pane again.

split.location: Editor area → Split editor divider: label on the collapsed strip between the two split editor panes; click to expand the hidden pane again. Keep very short (may be shown stacked letter by letter).

actual_label.location: Query plans → Plan kind name (actual): name of the actual execution plan (statement executes), inserted into plan capture status messages such as “Capturing {plan}…” and the plan summary; short noun.

capture_failed.location: Workbench → Status bar and Results → Execution plan pane: error shown when the request to capture an execution plan failed on the server; {error} is the server message.

capture_in_progress.location: Workbench → Status bar: info message shown when Explain is triggered while a plan capture is still running for the same query tab; the running capture continues.
capture_in_progress.value: Ya hay una captura de plan en curso

capturing.location: Workbench → Status bar: busy message while an execution plan is captured without running the statement; {plan} is the plan kind name (Estimated, Actual, or Profile).

capturing_executes.location: Workbench → Status bar: busy message while an execution plan is captured by actually running a data-changing statement; warns that it executes; {plan} is the plan kind name (Actual or Profile).

clipboard_empty.location: Workbench → Status bar: info message shown when Paste Plan from Clipboard is used but the clipboard holds no text, or only blank text.

clipboard_source.location: Query plans → Imported plan: lowercase word naming the clipboard as the source of a pasted plan; fills {source} in “imported: {source}”.

connect_database.location: Toolbar and Query menu → Explain actions: disabled-state tooltip and status message shown when no database connection is active, so no execution plan can be captured.
connect_database.value: Conéctate a una base de datos para capturar un plan de ejecución

connect_options.location: Toolbar → Explain options popover: fallback header line used in place of the server version when no connection is active; prompts to connect before choosing Explain options.
connect_options.value: Conéctate para configurar las opciones de Explain

connect_server.location: Workbench → Status bar: info message shown when Explain (estimated or actual plan) is triggered by shortcut or menu with no active server connection.
connect_server.value: Conéctate a un servidor para capturar un plan de ejecución

document_parse_error.location: Results → Execution plan pane: error prefix when one of several plan documents returned by the server could not be parsed; {index} is the failing document’s number, {total} the document count, {error} the parser message.

estimated_label.location: Query plans → Plan kind name (estimated): name of the estimated execution plan (optimizer only, statement never runs), inserted into plan capture status messages and the plan summary; short noun.

file_fallback.location: Query plans → Open Plan…: generic lowercase word used as the plan’s source name when the chosen file’s name cannot be read; fills {source} in “imported: {source}”.

file_read_failed.location: Workbench → Status bar: error shown when Open Plan… cannot read the chosen plan file; {path} is the full file path, {error} the operating-system error.

import_failed.location: Workbench → Status bar: error shown when an opened or pasted plan was recognized but could not be parsed; {error} is the parser message.
import_failed.value: No se pudo leer el plan: {error}

import_summary_finding_singular.location: Workbench → Status bar: success message after opening or pasting a plan with several statements and exactly one finding; {dialect} is the plan format, {statement_count} statements, {finding_count} is 1.

import_summary_plural.location: Workbench → Status bar: success message after opening or pasting a plan with several statements and zero or several findings; {dialect} is the plan format, {statement_count} and {finding_count} are counts.

import_summary_singular.location: Workbench → Status bar: success message after opening or pasting a plan with exactly one statement and exactly one finding; {dialect} is the plan format; both counts are 1.

import_summary_statement_singular.location: Workbench → Status bar: success message after opening or pasting a plan with exactly one statement and zero or several findings; {dialect} is the plan format, {finding_count} the number of findings.

imported_context.location: Results → Execution plan pane: source label recorded for a plan loaded with Open Plan… or Paste Plan instead of the query SQL, used to keep plan comparisons apart; {source} is the file name or “clipboard”.

no_active_tab.location: Workbench → Status bar: error shown when Explain is triggered but there is no open query tab to take SQL from.

no_sql.location: Workbench → Status bar: info message shown when Explain (estimated or actual plan) is triggered but the active query editor is empty.

open_file_prompt.location: Open Plan… file chooser → Dialog title: title of the system open-file dialog for loading a saved execution plan; lists the accepted file types (.sqlplan, .json, .xml).

open_file_unavailable.location: Browser preview → Status bar: name of the Open Plan… feature, inserted into the message explaining that it is not available in the browser version.
open_file_unavailable.value: Abrir un archivo de plan no está disponible

parse_failed_status.location: Workbench → Status bar: error shown when the execution plan returned by the server could not be parsed; details appear in the execution plan pane.
parse_failed_status.value: No se pudo analizar el plan de ejecución

parse_failed_viewer.location: Results → Execution plan pane: error message shown in the pane when the captured plan could not be parsed; {error} is the parser detail.

profile_capture_in_progress.location: Workbench → Profile Query execution-plan capture: status shown when another plan capture is already running.
profile_capture_in_progress.value: Ya hay una captura de plan en curso

profile_connect_server.location: Workbench → Profile Query execution-plan capture: status shown when no server connection is active.
profile_connect_server.value: Conéctate a un servidor para capturar un plan de ejecución

profile_label.location: Query plans → Plan kind name (profile): name of the Profile plan kind (runs a SELECT with ANALYZE-style profiling), inserted into capture status messages and plan summaries; short noun.

profile_no_active_tab.location: Workbench → Profile Query execution-plan capture: error shown when no query tab is active.

profile_no_sql.location: Workbench → Profile Query execution-plan capture: status shown when the active query contains no SQL.

profile_select_only.location: Workbench → Status bar: error shown when Explain with Profile is used on a statement that is not a plain SELECT; {reason} says why the statement was refused; suggests the Estimated plan for writes.
profile_select_only.value: Perfil ejecuta la instrucción con ANALYZE; solo analiza instrucciones SELECT ({reason}). Usa Estimado para escrituras.

server_returned_none.location: Workbench → Status bar and Results → Execution plan pane: error shown when the plan capture query finished but the server sent back no execution plan.
server_returned_none.value: El servidor no devolvió ningún plan de ejecución.

summary_finding_singular.location: Workbench → Status bar: success message after a plan capture with several statements and exactly one finding; {plan} is the plan kind (Estimated, Actual, Profile), {statement_count} statements, {finding_count} is 1.

summary_plural.location: Workbench → Status bar: success message after a plan capture with several statements and zero or several findings; {plan} is the plan kind, {statement_count} and {finding_count} are counts.

summary_singular.location: Workbench → Status bar: success message after a plan capture with exactly one statement and exactly one finding; {plan} is the plan kind (Estimated, Actual, Profile); both counts are 1.

summary_statement_singular.location: Workbench → Status bar: success message after a plan capture with exactly one statement and zero or several findings; {plan} is the plan kind, {finding_count} the number of findings.

unrecognised_format.location: Workbench → Status bar: error shown when an opened or pasted plan is in none of the supported formats; the list of formats is technical and should keep its product names.
unrecognised_format.value: Formato de plan no reconocido (se esperaba ShowPlan XML, JSON de PostgreSQL/MySQL, MySQL TREE o filas de SQLite EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN)

unsupported_engine.location: Workbench → Status bar: info message shown when a plan shortcut is used on a database engine with no execution plan support; {engine} is the database type name.
unsupported_engine.value: Los planes de consulta están desactivados para este tipo de base de datos ({engine}).

version_unknown.location: Toolbar → Explain options popover: fallback header line shown when connected to an engine without plan support and no more specific reason is available; means the server version is unknown.

cancelled.location: Workbench → Status bar → Procedure mode run result: message shown when the user cancels a Procedure mode deploy or run before it finishes.

deploy_failed.location: Workbench → Status bar → Procedure mode run result: error when the CREATE/ALTER statement that deploys the procedure (or its existence probe) fails; {error} is the server’s error message.

deploying.location: Workbench → Status bar: busy message when Procedure mode runs, while the procedure in the editor is created or altered on the server before being called; {name} is the procedure’s qualified name.

execution_failed.location: Workbench → Status bar → Procedure mode run result: error when the procedure deployed but running it with the entered parameters failed; {error} is the server’s error message.

finished.location: Workbench → Status bar → Procedure mode run result: success message after the procedure was deployed (committed) and then executed; {name} is the procedure’s qualified name and {elapsed_ms} the execution time in milliseconds.
finished.value: Se desplegó {name} y se ejecutó en {elapsed_ms} ms

finished_rolled_back.location: Workbench → Status bar → Procedure mode run result: success message after a run with Rollback checked, where the deploy and execution were rolled back afterwards; {name} is the procedure’s qualified name and {elapsed_ms} the execution time in milliseconds.
finished_rolled_back.value: Se desplegó {name} (revertido) y se ejecutó en {elapsed_ms} ms

header_invalid.location: Query tab → Procedure mode parameter strip: note shown when the procedure header in the editor cannot be parsed; {error} is the parse error; explains that Run will execute the editor text as-is.
header_invalid.value: No se puede analizar el encabezado del procedimiento ({error}). Ejecutar ejecuta el búfer sin cambios.

no_parameters.location: Query tab → Procedure mode parameter strip: note shown in the header row when the parsed procedure declares no parameters, so there is nothing to fill in.

not_procedure.location: Query tab → Procedure mode parameter strip: note shown when Procedure mode is on but the editor text is not a CREATE or ALTER PROCEDURE script; Run executes the text unchanged.
not_procedure.value: No es un script de procedimiento. Ejecutar ejecuta el búfer sin cambios.

parameter_invalid.location: Workbench → Status bar: error shown when Procedure mode refuses to run because a parameter value in the strip is invalid; {name} is the parameter name (shown after @), {error} the validation message.

read_only_table_parameter.location: Query tab → Procedure mode parameter strip: note in place of a value input for a read-only table-valued parameter, explaining an empty table is passed when the procedure is called.
read_only_table_parameter.value: Parámetro de tabla de solo lectura; se pasa una tabla vacía

returned.location: Query tab → Procedure mode parameter strip → header row: text shown after a run with the procedure’s return value; {code} is the return code. Lowercase fragment.

rollback.location: Query tab → Procedure mode parameter strip → header row: checkbox label; when checked, deploy and call run inside one transaction that is rolled back afterwards, so nothing is kept.

run_failed.location: Workbench → Status bar → Procedure mode run result: error after a Rollback-checked run whose combined deploy-and-execute batch failed; {error} is the server’s error message.

unsupported_with_default.location: Query tab → Procedure mode parameter strip: note in place of a value input for a parameter whose data type cannot be edited, explaining the parameter’s declared default value will be used.
unsupported_with_default.value: Tipo no admitido; se usa el valor predeterminado declarado

unsupported_without_default.location: SQLLY → Workbench → Procedure parameter strip → unsupported parameter without a declared default: note explaining that no value can be supplied.
unsupported_without_default.value: Tipo no admitido; no se puede proporcionar ningún valor

lock_now.location: Query workspace → Production banner: small button shown while writes are temporarily unlocked on a production connection; ends the unlock immediately and returns the connection to read-only.

read_only_banner.location: Query workspace → Production banner: warning text in the strip under the tab bar when the active connection is marked production and writes are locked; keep the uppercase marker style.

unlock_fifteen_minutes.location: Query workspace → Production banner: small button that allows writes on the read-only production connection for fifteen minutes; the third of three unlock durations.

unlock_five_minutes.location: Query workspace → Production banner: small button that allows writes on the read-only production connection for five minutes; the second of three unlock durations.

unlock_one_minute.location: Query workspace → Production banner: small button that allows writes on the read-only production connection for one minute; the first of three unlock durations.

unlocked_banner.location: Query workspace → Production banner: warning text in the strip under the tab bar while writes are temporarily unlocked on a production connection; {remaining} is the remaining unlock time.

capture_actual_plan.location: Query toolbar → More query tools menu: item that captures the actual execution plan of the editor’s SQL (the statement runs); disabled with a reason when plans are unavailable.

edit_connection.location: Query toolbar → More query tools menu: first item, opens the connection editor for the active connection.

overflow_tooltip.location: Query toolbar → Overflow menu button tooltip: tooltip on the vertical three-dot button that opens the menu of extra query tools and toggles.

new_name_placeholder.location: Rename dialog (Object Explorer → Rename): placeholder in the text input where the user types the object’s new name.

open_script_button.location: Rename dialog (Object Explorer → Rename): button that opens the generated rename script in a new query tab for review; nothing runs from the dialog.
open_script_button.value: Abrir script de cambio de nombre

preview_notice.location: Rename dialog (Object Explorer → Rename): dimmed note above the SQL preview explaining that the script only opens in a new tab and that objects referencing the old name are not updated.
preview_notice.value: Vista previa: el script se abre en una pestaña nueva para revisarlo y no se ejecuta desde aquí. Cambiar el nombre no actualiza los objetos que hacen referencia al nombre anterior.

script_opened_status.location: Workbench → Status bar: info message after the Rename dialog opened its rename script in a new query tab; reminds the user to review the script and then run it.
script_opened_status.value: Script de cambio de nombre abierto: revísalo y después ejecútalo

title.location: Rename dialog (Object Explorer → Rename): dialog title; {name} is the current name of the table, view, or other object being renamed.

cached_banner.location: Results → Cached results banner: strip above results restored from the local cache when a query tab reopens; {timestamp} is when that query finished; tells the user to re-run for fresh data.
cached_banner.value: Resultados en caché de {timestamp}: vuelve a ejecutar para actualizar

computed_column_snapshot.location: Workbench → Status bar: info message shown when a computed column from the results formula bar cannot be written into the query because the tab is a read-only snapshot.
computed_column_snapshot.value: La columna se agregó a estos resultados; la consulta de esta pestaña de instantánea no se puede editar.

computed_column_written.location: Workbench → Status bar: success message after a computed column defined in the results formula bar was written into the query as a column directive comment.
computed_column_written.value: Columna calculada escrita en la consulta como -- sqlly column: — ⌘Z la deshace.

lock_already_matches.location: Workbench → Status bar: info message shown when the Results lock button is clicked but the query’s lock block already reproduces the results exactly, so nothing changed.
lock_already_matches.value: El bloqueo de la consulta ya coincide con los resultados.

lock_snapshot_read_only.location: Workbench → Results → Lock Results action: refusal shown when results already come from a read-only snapshot.
lock_snapshot_read_only.value: Esta pestaña es una instantánea de solo lectura, por lo que su consulta no se puede editar.

locked.location: Workbench → Status bar: success message after the Results lock button wrote the grid’s columns, widths, formatting, pivot and chart into the query; mentions the undo shortcut (⌘Z).
locked.value: Resultados bloqueados en la consulta: la próxima ejecución será exactamente igual. ⌘Z lo deshace.

locked_with_notes.location: Workbench → Status bar: success message after locking results into the query when some settings could not be written; points to the Messages tab for details and mentions the undo shortcut (⌘Z).
locked_with_notes.value: Resultados bloqueados en la consulta; consulta Mensajes para ver lo que una directiva no puede incluir. ⌘Z lo deshace.

settings_already_applied.location: Workbench → Status bar: info message shown when Result Settings or the result name menu asks for settings the query already contains; {result_set} is the result set’s number.
settings_already_applied.value: La consulta ya tiene esta configuración para Resultados {result_set}.

settings_updated.location: Workbench → Status bar: success message after Result Settings or the result name menu wrote directive comments into the query; {result_set} is the result set’s number; mentions undo (⌘Z).
settings_updated.value: Configuración de la consulta actualizada para Resultados {result_set}: ⌘Z lo deshace.

snapshot_read_only.location: Workbench → Status bar: info message shown when Result Settings or the result name menu tries to change the query of a tab that is a read-only results snapshot.
snapshot_read_only.value: Esta pestaña es una instantánea de solo lectura, por lo que su consulta no se puede editar.

statement_commented_out.location: Workbench → Status bar: success message after the result name menu commented out the statement that produced a result set; {result_set} is its number; mentions undo (⌘Z).
statement_commented_out.value: Instrucción comentada para Resultados {result_set}: ⌘Z la recupera.

auth_token_credentials.location: Resume Connection dialog → Connection details → Credentials row: value shown when the remembered connection signs in with an authentication token instead of a user name, so no account name can be displayed.

cancel_button.location: Resume Connection dialog → Footer: secondary button beside “Switch” that closes the prompt without switching to the tab’s remembered connection; the query is not run.

credentials_label.location: Resume Connection dialog → Connection details: row label for the account or sign-in method of the remembered connection (user name, “Integrated credentials”, or “Authentication token”).

database_label.location: Resume Connection dialog → Connection details: row label for the database the restored query tab was last run against, shown under the Server row.

default_database.location: Workbench → Resume Connection dialog: database detail value shown when the remembered connection has no explicit database.

disabled_scope_tooltip.location: Workbench → Query toolbar → Query resume toggle: tooltip shown when the query resume scope in Settings is set to none, so the toggle is disabled; {scope} is that scope name.
disabled_scope_tooltip.value: La reanudación del estado de la consulta está desactivada (ámbito: {scope}). Cambia el ámbito en Preferencias para activar la reanudación por consulta.

disconnected_explanation.location: Resume Connection dialog → Disconnected explanation line: small dimmed explanatory line under the switch question, explaining that SQLLY is currently disconnected and the tab remembers a previous connection.
disconnected_explanation.value: No estás conectado. Esta consulta se ejecutó por última vez en la conexión de arriba.

dont_ask_again.location: Resume Connection dialog → Footer: checkbox label at the left; when checked, later runs in this tab switch to the remembered connection automatically without asking.

environment_label.location: Resume Connection dialog → Connection details: row label for the environment tag (for example Production or Development) of the saved connection the tab would switch to.

following_off_tooltip.location: Workbench → Query toolbar → Query resume toggle: tooltip when saving query state is off for this tab because it follows the global scope from Settings; {scope} is that scope name.
following_off_tooltip.value: Guardar el estado de esta consulta: desactivado (según el ámbito: {scope})

following_on_tooltip.location: Workbench → Query toolbar → Query resume toggle: tooltip when saving query state is on for this tab because it follows the global scope from Settings; {scope} is that scope name.
following_on_tooltip.value: Guardar el estado de esta consulta: activado (según el ámbito: {scope})

forced_off_tooltip.location: Workbench → Query toolbar → Query resume toggle: tooltip when the user has turned saving query state off for this tab, overriding the global scope; {scope} is that scope name.
forced_off_tooltip.value: Guardar el estado de esta consulta: desactivado a la fuerza (sustituye el ámbito: {scope})

forced_on_tooltip.location: Workbench → Query toolbar → Query resume toggle: tooltip when the user has turned saving query state on for this tab, overriding the global scope; {scope} is that scope name.
forced_on_tooltip.value: Guardar el estado de esta consulta: activado a la fuerza (sustituye el ámbito: {scope})

integrated_credentials.location: Resume Connection dialog → Connection details → Credentials row: value shown when the remembered connection uses Windows/integrated authentication rather than a named login.

server_label.location: Resume Connection dialog → Connection details: first row label, for the server host name the restored query tab was last connected to.

switch_button.location: Resume Connection dialog → Footer: primary button that connects to the tab’s remembered server and database and then runs the query; verb meaning “switch over”.

switch_prompt.location: Resume Connection dialog → Switch prompt: main question shown when you run a restored query tab while disconnected; {server} is the remembered server name and {database} the remembered database.

title.location: Resume Connection dialog → Title bar: dialog title, shown when running a reopened query tab while disconnected and the tab remembers the connection it last used.

unknown_credentials.location: Workbench → Resume Connection dialog → Credentials detail: fallback shown when no saved profile can be resolved.

unknown_environment.location: Workbench → Resume Connection dialog → Environment detail: fallback shown when no saved profile can be resolved.

connect_to_copy_update.location: Workbench → Status bar: message shown when Results grid context menu → Copy As → SQL UPDATE is used while no database is connected; means connect first to copy the rows as UPDATE statements.
connect_to_copy_update.value: Conéctate a una base de datos para copiar instrucciones UPDATE.

connect_to_insert.location: Workbench → Status bar: message shown when Results grid row context menu → Batch Insert is chosen while no database is connected; means connect first to insert rows.
connect_to_insert.value: Conéctate a una base de datos para insertar filas.

connect_to_paste.location: Workbench → Status bar: message shown when pasting (Cmd+V) clipboard rows into the Results grid while no database is connected; means connect first to paste rows into the table.
connect_to_paste.value: Conéctate a una base de datos para pegar filas.

connect_to_stage_deletes.location: Workbench → Status bar: message shown when Stage Delete is chosen for several selected Results grid rows while no database is connected.
connect_to_stage_deletes.value: Conéctate a una base de datos para marcar filas para eliminación

copied_update_plural.location: Workbench → Status bar: confirmation after Results grid → Copy As → SQL UPDATE copied several rows to the clipboard; plural form, {count} is the number of UPDATE statements copied.

copied_update_singular.location: Workbench → Status bar: confirmation after Results grid → Copy As → SQL UPDATE copied one row to the clipboard; singular form, {count} is 1.

saved_refresh_hint.location: Workbench → Status bar: success message after a row edit is saved when the original query is not a plain SELECT, so SQLLY does not re-run it automatically to refresh the grid.
saved_refresh_hint.value: Fila guardada. Vuelve a ejecutar la consulta para actualizar la cuadrícula.

staged_delete_plural.location: Workbench → Status bar: message after several selected Results grid rows are marked as pending deletes (not yet saved); plural form, {count} is the number of rows.

staged_delete_singular.location: Workbench → Status bar: message after one Results grid row is marked as a pending delete (not yet saved); singular form, {count} is 1.

run_plural.location: Run Statements dialog → Footer: primary button label when several statements are checked; runs only the checked statements as one batch. {count} is how many are checked.

run_singular.location: Run Statements dialog → Footer: primary button label when exactly one statement is checked; runs just that statement. {count} is 1.

run_without_selection.location: Run Statements dialog → Footer: primary button label shown when no statement is checked; clicking it only reports that a statement must be selected.

select_all.location: Run Statements dialog → Footer: button at the left that checks every statement in the list.

select_none.location: Run Statements dialog → Footer: button beside “Select all” that unchecks every statement in the list; short word meaning “select none”.

selection_required.location: Workbench → Status bar: message shown when the Run button in the Run Statements dialog is clicked with no statements checked; the dialog stays open.

title.location: Run Statements dialog → Title bar: dialog title; opened by the “Run Statements…” command, it lists each statement in the editor with a checkbox so you can pick which ones to run.

day.location: Workbench → Refresh schema button tooltips: age phrase for a schema snapshot pulled exactly one day ago (singular); fills {age} in the timestamp line.

days.location: Workbench → Refresh schema button tooltips: age phrase for a schema snapshot pulled two or more days ago (plural); fills {age} in the timestamp line.

hour.location: Workbench → Refresh schema button tooltips: age phrase for a schema snapshot pulled about one hour ago (singular); fills {age} in the timestamp line.

hours.location: Workbench → Refresh schema button tooltips: age phrase for a schema snapshot pulled two to 23 hours ago (plural); fills {age} in the timestamp line.

just_now.location: Workbench → Refresh schema button tooltips: age phrase for a schema snapshot pulled less than a minute ago; fills {age} in the timestamp line.

minute.location: Workbench → Refresh schema button tooltips: age phrase for a schema snapshot pulled about one minute ago (singular); fills {age} in the timestamp line.

minutes.location: Workbench → Refresh schema button tooltips: age phrase for a schema snapshot pulled two to 59 minutes ago (plural); fills {age} in the timestamp line.

timestamp.location: Workbench → Refresh schema button tooltips: snapshot age text inserted after “last pulled”; {timestamp} is the local date and time (yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm), {age} the relative age such as “Just now”.

ai_pending.location: Confirm Staged Changes dialog → AI review pending note: dimmed note under the SQL preview while the required AI review of the pending changes is still running; Save stays disabled until it finishes.

ai_wait.location: Workbench → Status bar: message shown if Save is attempted in Confirm Staged Changes before the AI review this connection requires has finished.
ai_wait.value: Esperando la revisión de IA: esta conexión la requiere antes de guardar los cambios pendientes

cancel.location: Confirm Staged Changes dialog → Footer: button between “Copy SQL” and “Save” that closes the dialog without saving; the staged changes stay pending in the grid.

cancelled_status.location: Workbench → Status bar: message shown after the Confirm Staged Changes dialog is cancelled or closed; nothing was written to the database.

commit_plural.location: Confirm Staged Changes dialog → Commit summary line (plural): summary line of what Save will do when several changes are pending; {count} is the number of changes, {table} the target table name.
commit_plural.value: Confirmar {count} cambios pendientes en {table} en una transacción

commit_singular.location: Confirm Staged Changes dialog → Commit summary line (singular): summary line of what Save will do when exactly one change is pending; {count} is 1, {table} the target table name.
commit_singular.value: Confirmar {count} cambio pendiente en {table} en una transacción

conflict_plural.location: Workbench → Status bar: error after saving staged changes is rolled back because one change matched an unexpected number of rows (zero or several); {statement_index} is the change number, {affected} the row count.
conflict_plural.value: El cambio {statement_index} afectó a {affected} filas; no se guardó nada

conflict_singular.location: Workbench → Status bar: singular form of the rolled-back save error, used when the reported row count is exactly one; {statement_index} is the change number, {affected} is 1. Nothing was saved.
conflict_singular.value: El cambio {statement_index} afectó a {affected} fila; no se guardó nada

copy_sql.location: Confirm Staged Changes dialog → Footer: first button, copies the SQL script for the pending changes to the clipboard without saving them.

production_read_only.location: Workbench → Status bar: error shown when saving staged grid changes on a Production connection whose writes are still locked; unlock writes first.
production_read_only.value: Las conexiones de producción son de solo lectura: desbloquea las escrituras antes de guardar los cambios pendientes

save.location: Confirm Staged Changes dialog → Footer: warning-colored primary button that commits all pending grid changes to the database in one transaction.

saved_status.location: Workbench → Status bar: success message after the pending grid changes were committed to the database and the grid refreshed.

table_fallback.location: Confirm Staged Changes dialog → Summary line: placeholder put in {table} when the target table name of the staged changes is unknown; keep the parentheses.

title.location: Confirm Staged Changes dialog → Title bar: dialog title, shown before saving pending grid edits when the connection requires confirmation, is read-only, or needs an AI review.

ready.location: Workbench → Status bar: initial idle message shown when SQLLY starts, before any query or action has reported a status.

terminal_launch_ready.location: Workbench → Open in Terminal flow: idle status restored while waiting for the terminal notice or after cancellation.

all_tabs_tooltip.location: Workbench → Query tab strip: tooltip on the chevron button at the right end that opens a searchable list of all open query tabs.

new_query_tooltip.location: Workbench → Query tab strip: tooltip on the plus button after the last tab that opens a new query tab; ⌘N is the keyboard shortcut.

search_placeholder.location: Workbench → Query tab strip → All tabs list: placeholder in the filter box at the top of the list, used to find an open tab by typing part of its name.

preview_empty_query.location: Workbench → Ctrl+Tab switcher → query preview: placeholder shown when the highlighted query editor contains no text.

preview_more_lines_plural.location: Workbench → Ctrl+Tab switcher → query preview: truncation marker when multiple SQL lines are omitted; {count} is the omitted line count.

preview_more_lines_singular.location: Workbench → Ctrl+Tab switcher → query preview: truncation marker when exactly one SQL line is omitted; {count} is 1.

preview_not_run.location: Workbench → Ctrl+Tab switcher → preview metadata: status shown when the highlighted query has never completed a run.

preview_ran_row_plural.location: Workbench → Ctrl+Tab switcher → preview metadata: completed query with zero or multiple result rows and at most one result set; {relative} is the localized elapsed time and {count} is the grouped row count.

preview_ran_row_plural_result_sets.location: Workbench → Ctrl+Tab switcher → preview metadata: completed query with zero or multiple rows and multiple result sets; {relative} is localized elapsed time, {count} is the grouped row count, and {result_set_count} is greater than 1.

preview_ran_row_singular.location: Workbench → Ctrl+Tab switcher → preview metadata: completed query with one result row and at most one result set; {relative} is the localized elapsed time and {count} is 1.

preview_ran_row_singular_result_sets.location: Workbench → Ctrl+Tab switcher → preview metadata: completed query with one result row and multiple result sets; {relative} is localized elapsed time, {count} is 1, and {result_set_count} is greater than 1.

relative_days_ago.location: Workbench → Ctrl+Tab switcher → preview metadata: relative completion time in whole days; {count} is the elapsed day count.

relative_hours_ago.location: Workbench → Ctrl+Tab switcher → preview metadata: relative completion time in whole hours; {count} is the elapsed hour count.

relative_just_now.location: Workbench → Ctrl+Tab switcher → preview metadata: relative completion time for a query that finished less than five seconds ago.

relative_minutes_ago.location: Workbench → Ctrl+Tab switcher → preview metadata: relative completion time in whole minutes; {count} is the elapsed minute count.

relative_seconds_ago.location: Workbench → Ctrl+Tab switcher → preview metadata: relative completion time in seconds; {count} is a whole number from 5 through 59.

clickhouse_native_forward_failed.location: Explorer → ClickHouse node → Open in Terminal: status-bar warning when a second SSH tunnel forward to ClickHouse's native-protocol port cannot be opened; {native_port} is the port number, {detail} the SSH library's own error text.
clickhouse_native_forward_failed.value: No se pudo abrir un reenvío del túnel al puerto nativo {native_port} de ClickHouse: {detail}

clickhouse_native_forward_missing.location: Explorer → ClickHouse node → Open in Terminal: status-bar warning for a tunneled ClickHouse connection when no tunnel forward to the native-protocol port exists for clickhouse-client.
clickhouse_native_forward_missing.value: clickhouse-client usa el protocolo nativo de ClickHouse, pero no se pudo abrir un reenvío del túnel al puerto nativo; abre una pestaña de consulta o conéctate sin el túnel.

duckdb_file_in_use.location: Explorer → DuckDB node → Open in Terminal: status-bar warning when SQLLY itself holds the DuckDB file open, so the duckdb client cannot take its lock.
duckdb_file_in_use.value: SQLLY tiene abierto este archivo de DuckDB, y DuckDB solo permite que un proceso use un archivo a la vez; desconecta esta conexión y cierra sus pestañas de consulta, y luego abre el terminal.

dump_tool_not_interactive.location: Explorer → Server node → Open in Terminal: status-bar warning when a backup tool was picked instead of an interactive client; {tool} is the tool name such as pg_dump. Internal safeguard, rarely seen.
dump_tool_not_interactive.value: {tool} es una herramienta de volcado, no una CLI interactiva

in_memory_no_file.location: Explorer → DuckDB or SQLite node → Open in Terminal: status-bar warning when the connection is in-memory and the command-line client has no database file to open.
in_memory_no_file.value: Esta conexión está en memoria; no hay ningún archivo que abrir

install_clickhouse_client.location: Explorer → ClickHouse node right-click menu → Open in Terminal: disabled menu item (and status-bar warning) when clickhouse-client is not installed on this computer.
install_clickhouse_client.value: Instala clickhouse-client para abrir un terminal

install_duckdb.location: Explorer → DuckDB node right-click menu → Open in Terminal: disabled menu item (and status-bar warning) when the duckdb command-line client is not installed on this computer.
install_duckdb.value: Instala duckdb para abrir un terminal

install_mysql.location: Explorer → MySQL or MariaDB node right-click menu → Open in Terminal: disabled menu item (and status-bar warning) when the mysql command-line client is not installed on this computer.
install_mysql.value: Instala el cliente de MySQL o MariaDB (mysql) para abrir un terminal

install_oracle.location: Explorer → Oracle node right-click menu → Open in Terminal: disabled menu item (and status-bar warning) when neither Oracle SQL*Plus nor SQLcl is installed on this computer.
install_oracle.value: Instala Oracle SQL*Plus o SQLcl para abrir un terminal

install_psql.location: Explorer → PostgreSQL node right-click menu → Open in Terminal: disabled menu item (and status-bar warning) when the psql command-line client is not installed on this computer.
install_psql.value: Instala el cliente de PostgreSQL (psql) para abrir un terminal

install_redis_cli.location: Explorer → Redis node right-click menu → Open in Terminal: disabled menu item (and status-bar warning) when the redis-cli command-line client is not installed on this computer.
install_redis_cli.value: Instala redis-cli (se incluye con Redis) para abrir un terminal

install_sqlcmd.location: Explorer → SQL Server node right-click menu → Open in Terminal: disabled menu item (and status-bar warning) when Microsoft's sqlcmd command-line tool is not installed on this computer.
install_sqlcmd.value: Instala sqlcmd (la herramienta de línea de comandos de SQL Server de Microsoft) para abrir un terminal

install_sqlite3.location: Explorer → SQLite node right-click menu → Open in Terminal: disabled menu item (and status-bar warning) when the sqlite3 command-line client is not installed on this computer.
install_sqlite3.value: Instala sqlite3 para abrir un terminal

invalid_program_path.location: Windows → Explorer → Server node → Open in Terminal: status-bar warning when the discovered command-line client path contains a quote character; {path} is that path.
invalid_program_path.value: {path} no es una ruta de programa válida

launcher_create_failed.location: Explorer → Server node → Open in Terminal: status-bar warning when the temporary launcher script for the terminal cannot be created; {detail} is the operating system's own error text.
launcher_create_failed.value: No se pudo crear el script de inicio: {detail}

launcher_write_failed.location: Explorer → Server node → Open in Terminal: status-bar warning when the temporary launcher script for the terminal cannot be written; {detail} is the operating system's own error text.
launcher_write_failed.value: No se pudo escribir el script de inicio: {detail}

no_terminal_emulator.location: Linux → Explorer → Server node → Open in Terminal: status-bar warning when none of the known terminal emulators could be started; {detail} lists each program tried with the operating system's error.
no_terminal_emulator.value: No se pudo iniciar ningún emulador de terminal ({detail})

note_clickhouse_custom_certificates.location: Explorer → ClickHouse node → Open in Terminal: caveat appended to the status-bar success message when the connection uses a custom CA or client certificate that clickhouse-client cannot take from SQLLY.
note_clickhouse_custom_certificates.value: clickhouse-client toma una CA o un certificado de cliente personalizados de su propio archivo de configuración (openSSL.client en ~/.clickhouse-client/config.xml), no de SQLLY.

note_clickhouse_native_forward.location: Explorer → ClickHouse node → Open in Terminal: caveat appended to the status-bar success message for an SSH-tunneled connection; {native_port} is the server's native port, {forward_port} the local forward port.
note_clickhouse_native_forward.value: clickhouse-client llega al puerto nativo {native_port} del servidor a través de un segundo reenvío en el túnel de esta conexión (127.0.0.1:{forward_port}); SQLLY lo mantiene abierto hasta que desconectes esta conexión o salgas; al desconectar se cierra y termina la sesión del terminal.

note_clickhouse_native_port_assumed.location: Explorer → ClickHouse node → Open in Terminal: caveat appended to the status-bar success message when the native-protocol port was guessed from the HTTP port; {native_port} is the guessed port, {http_port} the connection's HTTP port.
note_clickhouse_native_port_assumed.value: clickhouse-client usa el protocolo nativo de ClickHouse, así que se conecta al puerto {native_port} (supuesto: el puerto {http_port} de esta conexión es HTTP; define el Puerto nativo en la conexión si el servidor usa otro).

note_clickhouse_native_port_configured.location: Explorer → ClickHouse node → Open in Terminal: caveat appended to the status-bar success message when the connection's Native port setting differs from its HTTP port; {native_port} is the native port, {http_port} the HTTP port.
note_clickhouse_native_port_configured.value: clickhouse-client usa el protocolo nativo de ClickHouse en el puerto {native_port} (el Puerto nativo de esta conexión); SQLLY usa HTTP en el {http_port}.

note_clickhouse_native_port_default.location: Explorer → ClickHouse node → Open in Terminal: caveat appended to the status-bar success message when the conventional native port is used alongside the HTTP port; {native_port} is the native port, {http_port} the HTTP port.
note_clickhouse_native_port_default.value: clickhouse-client usa el protocolo nativo de ClickHouse en el puerto {native_port}; SQLLY usa HTTP en el {http_port}.

note_clickhouse_tunnel_certificate.location: Explorer → ClickHouse node → Open in Terminal: caveat appended to the status-bar success message when an SSH-tunneled connection verifies the server certificate.
note_clickhouse_tunnel_certificate.value: A través del túnel SSH, clickhouse-client comprueba el certificado del servidor con 127.0.0.1; si rechaza el certificado, confía en el certificado del servidor en esta conexión o conéctate sin el túnel.

note_cloud_iam_password_prompt.location: Explorer → Server node → Open in Terminal: caveat appended to the status-bar success message for AWS/GCP IAM connections; {tool} is the command-line client name such as psql.
note_cloud_iam_password_prompt.value: {tool} pedirá una contraseña: los tokens de IAM en la nube se generan cuando SQLLY se conecta y no se pasan al terminal.

note_mariadb_tunnel_unverified.location: Explorer → MariaDB node → Open in Terminal: caveat appended to the status-bar success message when the connection uses an SSH tunnel and full certificate verification.
note_mariadb_tunnel_unverified.value: A través del túnel SSH, el cliente mariadb no puede comprobar el nombre de host del servidor, así que la sesión del terminal está cifrada pero el certificado no se verifica.

note_mysql_missing_ca.location: Explorer → MySQL node → Open in Terminal: caveat appended to the status-bar success message when certificate verification is on but no CA file could be found for the mysql client.
note_mysql_missing_ca.value: El cliente mysql necesita un archivo de CA para verificar el certificado del servidor y no se encontró ninguno; la sesión del terminal está cifrada pero sin verificar. Añade un archivo de CA en los ajustes TLS de la conexión para verificarlo.

note_mysql_tunnel_chain_only.location: Explorer → MySQL node → Open in Terminal: caveat appended to the status-bar success message when the connection uses an SSH tunnel and full certificate verification.
note_mysql_tunnel_chain_only.value: A través del túnel SSH, el cliente mysql no puede comprobar el nombre de host del servidor, así que solo verifica la cadena de certificados.

note_sqlcmd_tunnel_certificate.location: Explorer → SQL Server node → Open in Terminal: caveat appended to the status-bar success message when an SSH-tunneled connection verifies certificates but the installed sqlcmd cannot name the real host.
note_sqlcmd_tunnel_certificate.value: A través del túnel SSH, sqlcmd comprueba el certificado del servidor con 127.0.0.1 (este sqlcmd no tiene el modificador -F de nombre de host en el certificado; go-sqlcmd 1.9+ y ODBC sqlcmd 18+ sí lo tienen); si rechaza el certificado, conéctate sin el túnel o confía en el certificado del servidor en esta conexión.

opened.location: Workbench → Open in Terminal → success status without caveats: message after the terminal starts; {name} is the connection name.

opened_with_notes.location: Workbench → Open in Terminal → completion status with caveats: message after the terminal starts; {name} is the connection name and {notes} contains the launch caveats.

opening.location: Workbench → Open in Terminal → launch status: busy message after confirmation when the terminal is being spawned; {name} is the connection name.

oracle_username_missing.location: Explorer → Oracle node → Open in Terminal: status-bar warning when the Oracle connection has no stored user name to hand to SQL*Plus.
oracle_username_missing.value: Las conexiones de Oracle necesitan un nombre de usuario para SQL*Plus; este perfil no tiene ninguno guardado

preparing.location: Workbench → Open in Terminal → preparation status: busy message while credentials, the CLI, and any tunnel are prepared; {name} is the connection name.

sandbox_blocked.location: Mac App Store edition → Explorer → Server node → Open in Terminal: status-bar warning when the App Store sandbox blocks launching a terminal program.
sandbox_blocked.value: Abrir en Terminal no está disponible en la edición de SQLLY para Mac App Store porque la zona de pruebas de la App Store no permite iniciar programas instalados en tu Mac. Consulta Ayuda ▸ Edición de Mac App Store para conocer las diferencias.

terminal_start_failed.location: Explorer → Server node → Open in Terminal: status-bar warning when the terminal application (Terminal.app or the Windows console) cannot be started; {detail} is the operating system's own error text.
terminal_start_failed.value: No se pudo iniciar un terminal: {detail}

tool_not_found.location: Explorer → Server node → Open in Terminal: status-bar warning when the command-line client disappeared between the menu check and the launch; {tool} is the program name such as psql.
tool_not_found.value: No se encontró {tool} en este equipo

tunnel_failed.location: Explorer → Server node → Open in Terminal: status-bar warning when the connection's SSH tunnel cannot be opened for the terminal; {detail} is the SSH library's own error text and stays untranslated.
tunnel_failed.value: No se pudo abrir el túnel SSH para el terminal: {detail}

unsupported_duckdb_in_memory.location: Explorer → DuckDB node right-click menu → Open in Terminal: disabled menu item (and status-bar warning) when the DuckDB connection is in-memory and has no database file for the duckdb client to open.
unsupported_duckdb_in_memory.value: Esta conexión de DuckDB está en memoria; no hay ningún archivo que abrir

unsupported_engine.location: Explorer → Server node right-click menu → Open in Terminal: disabled menu item (and status-bar warning) when the connection's database engine has no command-line client SQLLY can open.
unsupported_engine.value: Abrir en Terminal no está disponible para este motor

unsupported_entra_sign_in.location: Explorer → SQL Server node right-click menu → Open in Terminal: disabled menu item (and status-bar warning) when the connection signs in with Microsoft Entra, which sqlcmd cannot take over.
unsupported_entra_sign_in.value: sqlcmd no puede usar el inicio de sesión de Entra de esta conexión; usa autenticación SQL o integrada

unsupported_libsql_http.location: Explorer → libSQL / Turso node right-click menu → Open in Terminal: disabled menu item (and status-bar warning) explaining libSQL speaks HTTP and pointing to the Turso CLI instead.
unsupported_libsql_http.value: libSQL / Turso usa HTTP; usa la CLI de Turso (turso db shell) para un terminal

unsupported_relay_route.location: Explorer → Server node right-click menu → Open in Terminal: disabled menu item (and status-bar warning) when the connection is reached through a relay bridge, so a local command-line client cannot dial it.
unsupported_relay_route.value: Abrir en Terminal necesita una conexión directa; esta pasa por un puente de retransmisión

unsupported_sqlite_in_memory.location: Explorer → SQLite node right-click menu → Open in Terminal: disabled menu item (and status-bar warning) when the SQLite connection is in-memory and has no database file for sqlite3 to open.
unsupported_sqlite_in_memory.value: Esta conexión de SQLite está en memoria; no hay ningún archivo que abrir

windows_line_break.location: Windows → Explorer → Server node → Open in Terminal: status-bar warning when a connection setting (host, user, database, file path) contains a line break the Windows command line cannot carry.
windows_line_break.value: Un ajuste de la conexión contiene un salto de línea, que una línea de comandos de Windows no admite.

cancel_button.location: Open in Terminal notice dialog → Footer: secondary button that closes the notice without writing the launcher script or opening Terminal.

cleanup_script.location: Workbench → Open in Terminal password notice → second bullet: launcher self-deletion before {tool} starts and fallback cleanup within {minutes} minutes.
cleanup_script.value: Su primera línea lo elimina antes de que se inicie {tool}. Si Terminal no lo ejecuta, SQLLY lo eliminará en un plazo de {minutes} minutos.

dont_show_again.location: Open in Terminal notice dialog → Footer: checkbox label at the left; when checked, this password-on-disk notice is not shown again for later terminal launches.

launcher_explanation.location: Workbench → Open in Terminal password notice → explanation: reason SQLLY uses a short launcher script to supply the password to Terminal.app.
launcher_explanation.value: Terminal.app no puede recibir la contraseña directamente de SQLLY, por lo que SQLLY la escribe en un pequeño script de inicio que Terminal ejecuta.

no_command_line_password.location: Workbench → Open in Terminal password notice → third bullet: assurance that the password is not exposed in command-line arguments visible through ps.
no_command_line_password.value: La contraseña nunca se incluye en la línea de comandos, por lo que otros procesos no pueden leerla con ps.

open_button.location: Open in Terminal notice dialog → Footer: primary button that writes the temporary launcher script and opens Terminal running the database command-line tool.

password_on_disk.location: Workbench → Open in Terminal password notice → headline: explanation that the saved password for connection {name} is briefly written to disk on macOS.
password_on_disk.value: En macOS, la contraseña de {name} se escribe temporalmente en el disco.

private_script.location: Workbench → Open in Terminal password notice → first bullet: filesystem permissions and private temporary location of the launcher script.
private_script.value: Solo tu usuario de macOS puede leer el script, que se encuentra en una carpeta temporal privada.

re_enable_hint.location: Workbench → Open in Terminal notice → footnote: explanation of where to re-enable the notice after choosing not to show it again.
re_enable_hint.value: Si ocultas esta nota, puedes volver a mostrarla en Configuración › Avanzado › Herramientas de base de datos.

remove_saved_password.location: Workbench → Open in Terminal password notice → fourth bullet: alternative of removing the saved connection password so {tool} prompts interactively instead.
remove_saved_password.value: Para evitar que se guarde en el disco, elimina la contraseña guardada de esta conexión y {tool} te la pedirá en el terminal.

title.location: Open in Terminal notice dialog → Title bar: title of the notice shown before Object Explorer’s Open in Terminal writes a connection password into a temporary launcher script on macOS.

ai_working.location: Workbench → Window title bar → Layout toggles: small dimmed indicator with a dot shown while an AI request is in progress, left of the output-panel toggle.

toggle_ai_tooltip.location: Workbench → Window title bar → Layout toggles: tooltip on the right-sidebar icon button that shows or hides the AI drawer.
toggle_ai_tooltip.value: Mostrar u ocultar el panel de IA

toggle_output_tooltip.location: Workbench → Window title bar → Layout toggles: tooltip on the bottom-panel icon button that shows or hides the results/output panel; ⌘J is the shortcut.
toggle_output_tooltip.value: Mostrar u ocultar el panel de salida (⌘J)

toggle_sidebar_tooltip.location: Workbench → Window title bar → Layout toggles: tooltip on the left-sidebar icon button that shows or hides the sidebar with the Object Explorer.
toggle_sidebar_tooltip.value: Mostrar u ocultar la barra lateral

activity_monitor_feature.location: Activity Monitor → Live tabs on a relay connection: noun phrase naming the Activity Monitor’s live capture, inserted as {feature} into the status-bar warning that the feature needs a direct connection rather than a relay bridge.

connect_admin_tool.location: Workbench → Status bar: info message shown when an admin tool is opened with no active connection, asking the user to connect first; {tool} is the tool’s name, such as Activity Monitor or Schema History.
connect_admin_tool.value: Conéctate a una base de datos para abrir {tool}

data_transfer_failed.location: Workbench → Status bar → Background tasks popover: failure state text on the Data Transfer task row, shown when the transfer between connections ends with an error.
data_transfer_failed.value: Error en la transferencia de datos

data_transfer_task_label.location: Workbench → Status bar → Background tasks popover: row label naming a running Data Transfer job (copying tables between connections) while it shows progress.

data_transfer_title.location: Tools → Data Transfer → Results window: title of the text output window that opens with the transfer summary after a data transfer finishes or fails.

database_search_unavailable.location: Browser-hosted SQLLY → Status bar: feature name inserted into the “not available in the browser” error when Search Database for Value is chosen in the browser build.
database_search_unavailable.value: La búsqueda de valores en la base de datos no está disponible

direct_route_required.location: Workbench → direct-database tool on a relay-routed connection: refusal explaining that {feature} requires a direct connection rather than the active relay bridge.
